Content covers: Abaye's own resolution that the mishnah teaches its own reasoning for why a handful taken at night may still be offered the next morning, since consecration in a service vessel is valid regardless of time and a handful, once designated, cannot revert to untithed status; the baraita's general classification of day-only versus night-eligible offerings and its own qualification distinguishing 'fit to be sacrificed' from 'consecrated so as to become disqualified' (with the extended disqualification list: one who immersed that day, one lacking atonement offerings, one who left the Temple courtyard, and remaining overnight, cross-referenced to Zevachim 87a); Rabbi Zeira's challenge from the showbread/frankincense-vessel mishnah and its own textual crux (with Rabbeinu Chananel's alternate reading disputing the word 'disqualified' itself); Rava's resolution reconciling the two baraitot by distinguishing night (not a lack of time, since the vessel could still consecrate the next morning) from day (a genuine lack of time, since an entire day must pass); and the extended discussion of the showbread's own Friday-night arrangement, whether removing it before dusk avoids disqualification, and the 'as if a monkey arranged it' principle for an arrangement made too early, closing into the ongoing washing/immersion principle continuing onto 30a.
